title: Safe source-control actions
summary: Agents MUST prepare reversible changes and MUST NOT perform irreversible source-control actions without explicit operator approval.
instructions: Agents MUST NOT run git push, gh pr create, gh pr merge, branch deletion, history rewrite, or destructive reset commands. The active invocation MUST record operator approval for that action first.
All commits MUST use the operator's Git identity as author and committer. Commit messages MUST describe only the changes and MUST NOT contain authorship attribution.
Agents commit and merge on their own judgment, on a branch that lands on `pan-dev`. Agents MUST NOT merge into `main`. The operator promotes `pan-dev` to `main` and pushes.

Nothing lands on `pan-dev` without a proper version. A change to any installable harness input (the payload `bin/install` copies, plus `config.json` and `.gitignore`) MUST reach `pan-dev` only inside a release. Each release MUST add exactly two commits to `pan-dev`: one squashed commit containing the complete change set and release metadata, followed by one commit indexing its hash. The `VERSION` MUST exceed the previous `pan-dev` version. Indexed installation and update behavior MUST remain valid. Agents MUST NOT commit an installable change directly on `pan-dev` or `main`.

Agents MUST land on `pan-dev` only through `pan release land`, which holds the mutex, integrates, allocates, verifies, and fast-forwards. Agents MUST NOT use `git merge`, `git update-ref`, or `pan worktree reconcile --into-branch pan-dev` as a substitute for `pan release land`.
Agents SHOULD preserve the pre-task workspace state and MUST record enough evidence to diagnose or revert a failed change.
A commit that closes a harness repair finding SHOULD name the intake file and the finding id. The next audit then reconciles that intake from the commit log.
